# bugs #3701: Error 91 for a second declaration of an extern object or of a function in one block

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3701/
- Category: [Fixes](../../fix.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17200
- Recommended action: Apply the patch and close. Related has a wrong-code fault of block-scope extern const objects on mcs51 that the patch does not fix.
- Patch: [bugs-3701.patch](../../patches/bugs-3701.patch), commit [`c686eaef9`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/c686eaef93200630125798675733442f02dec931). Applies to r17200 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

Two block-scope `extern` declarations of one object in one block get error 91, "extern definition
for 'name_data' mismatches with declaration", and error 177. Two declarations of one function in
a block get these errors too. C11 6.7 paragraph 3 limits identifiers without linkage to one
declaration in a scope, and these identifiers have linkage.

A second form gets error 91 for the first declaration of a block. With `int a[2];` at file scope
and `extern int a[];` in a block, a further `extern int a[];` in a nested block gets it.

Both forms were reproduced for mcs51 on r17193 with the earlier patches of this report. The front
end reports the errors, so they do not depend on the port.

## Cause

`addSymChain` in `src/SDCCsymt.c` has two faults. When the block already has a symbol of the
name, it sets its error flag for every symbol that is not a parameter, and it does not test
whether the two declarations have linkage.

For a block-scope `extern` declaration, `addSymChain` tests whether a declaration without linkage
is visible. The test reads the `extern` flag with `IS_EXTERN (csym->type)`, from the first link of
the type, and that link has the flag only when the type does not have a declarator. A visible
block-scope `extern` declaration of an array, a pointer, or a function therefore counts as a
declaration without linkage. `addSymChain` then compares the new declaration with the file-scope
declaration by `compareTypeExact`, by which `extern int a[];` is not equal to `int a[2];`.

## Fix

When both symbols have the `extern` flag and the second declaration does not have an initializer,
`addSymChain` completes the array length and the prototype in both types and compares the types
with `compareTypeExact`, as it does for two declarations at file scope. `prepareDeclarationSymbol`
sets the flag for functions that a block declares without a storage-class specifier. A second
declaration that has an initializer gets error 91 with and without the patch. The test for a
visible declaration without linkage reads the flag from `csym->etype`.

The symbol of the first declaration stays in the symbol table, because `resolveSymbols` finds the
symbol of an expression by level, block, and sequence point, and expressions between the two
declarations need it. `addSymChain` takes the symbol of the second declaration out of the chain,
and the actions of the two `declaration_list` rules in `src/SDCC.y` call it before they append the
chain to the list of the block.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-3701.c` declares objects, arrays, and functions two or three times
in a block, in one case through a macro as in the ticket. On r17193 it does not compile for
mcs51-small, mcs51-large, mcs51-small-stack-auto, and mcs51-large-stack-auto, the four variants
that were run. With the patch it passes on host, the six mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80.
`support/valdiag/tests/bug-3701.c` has 8 cases. Three must compile. Five must get an error: two
pairs of `extern` declarations with incompatible types, and three pairs of an `extern` declaration
and a variable or a parameter of that name in the block.

For mcs51-small, the code size and the tick count of every other regression test are equal with
and without the patch. With the series of this report up to the patch for #4159 applied to
r17193, the regression suite has 0 failures for host, the six mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80. The
diagnostics suite has 0 failures for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8.

## Related

These faults are present on r17193 and with the patch.

- On mcs51, objects that a block declares `extern const` are read from data memory.
  `unsigned char f(void) { extern const unsigned char table[4]; return table[2]; }` compiles to
  `mov dpl,(_table + 0x0002)`. The example of the ticket has this form. With the patch it
  compiles, and a read of `name_data[1]` uses `mov` through the block-scope declaration and `movc`
  through a file-scope declaration. `checkSClass` in `src/SDCCsymt.c` gives const objects the
  storage class of code memory only at file scope or when they are static. A change there was not
  tested.
- Functions that access one object through two symbols get wrong code.
  `int counter; int f(void) { counter = 5; { extern int counter; counter++; } return counter; }`
  returns 5 on mcs51, and a test of this form also failed on stm8 and ucz80. The cause was not
  looked for. With the patch, two declarations in one block give correct code, because one symbol
  remains.
- `typedef int t; typedef int t;` in a block gets error 0, Duplicate symbol. At file scope the
  compiler accepts the two lines.
